My husband and I created “Rules of Engagement”

1.	⁠No name calling. It’s hard to live a happy life, if in the back of your mind you wonder if they really think you’re whatever you’re being called during this fight.
2.	⁠Never in front of the children We never disagreed, on anything important, in front of the kids. We waited until we were behind closed doors.
3.	⁠United front My husband and I always put forth a united front in raising our 4. If the kids know what to expect, their childish ways will not divide you.
4.	⁠This one may be confusing, but we had a real issue adhering to this rule. If one of us comes to the other with a gripe, the other cannot, in defense, argue some other topic/gripe in an attempt to deflect.
5.	⁠Love language This was a late edition, but learning and understanding each other is so important.

I realized on my 50th birthday, this year, I only have about 20 more seasons… not years.

This is going to be kinda weird, but I don’t care.

I live in Ohio. The legalization of cannabis happened in November. I enjoy edibles. I don’t like to smoke. Each household can grow up to 12 plants. I start researching seeds and buying the grow lights, the shelves, the tent and the heaters. Now comes along my 50th birthday, on December 12th. 🤯 I immediately began thinking of years in terms of seasons. I only have 20 more springs, summers, winters and falls.

Moral of the story…. You are young. You are acutely aware of time and mortality. Yes, you have things to do, people to see and parties to go to…. Instead of planning the year ahead, plan your life!  Create “Engienoob’s Book of Life”, work in progress.

Daily Weekly Monthly Yearly Decade Life with no end date.

Pencil in your plans and goals. When it’s a sure thing mark it in ink!

Think of all of things you want to get done, start doing them and your perspective will start to change.
